assertion_results.text: The query-scope analysis identifies that the task targets a subset — specifically 'SPDX SBOMs' not all SBOMs — by extracting subset-indicating language from the Description section
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md section 1 'Subset-restricting language found in the task' quotes the Description: "iterate over each **SPDX** SBOM document"; "**Only SPDX SBOMs** need re-processing — CycloneDX documents already have supplier information populated". It concludes: "Target scope: SBOM records whose type is SPDX — a type qualifier, i.e. a strict subset of the `sbom` table. 'All' in 'all SPDX SBOMs' means all records within that subset, not all SBOMs."

assertion_results.text: The query-scope analysis verifies that the sbom entity's labels column (jsonb) supports filtering by document type at the database level, rather than requiring application-level filtering
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md section 2 'Available filter at the data source': "`entity/src/sbom.rs` has a `labels` column (`jsonb`). SPDX rows carry {\"type\": \"spdx\"}; CycloneDX rows carry {\"type\": \"cyclonedx\"}. So the subset can be expressed directly in the query: WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx'". Section 4: "a narrower query **is** possible at the data source through the `labels` jsonb column."

assertion_results.text: The plan uses a filtered query to select only SPDX documents (e.g., WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx' or equivalent ORM filter) instead of loading all documents and discarding CycloneDX ones in application code
assertion_results.evidence: plan.md migration code: `sbom::Entity::find().select_only().column(sbom::Column::SbomId).filter(Expr::cust("labels->>'type' = 'spdx'")).into_tuple().all(db)`, and SQL section: `SELECT sbom_id FROM sbom WHERE labels->>'type' = 'spdx';` with note "CycloneDX rows ... are never selected, so their source documents are never fetched or parsed."

assertion_results.text: The plan or query-scope analysis explicitly mentions the performance impact of loading all documents — referencing that production environments have hundreds of thousands of non-target CycloneDX records
assertion_results.evidence: query-scope.md section 1 cites production has "hundreds of thousands of CycloneDX documents alongside a smaller number of SPDX documents"; section 4 table row for unfiltered: "All (hundreds of thousands, mostly CycloneDX)"; and "Performance: the cost moves from O(all SBOMs) document I/O and parsing to O(SPDX SBOMs). Production is dominated by CycloneDX, so this cuts most of the I/O."

assertion_results.text: The plan does NOT propose using an unfiltered query like Sbom::find() or Document::all() followed by an application-level type check to discard CycloneDX documents
assertion_results.evidence: Unfiltered approach appears only as rejected: query-scope.md "Rejected alternative: `sbom::Entity::find().all(db)` (i.e. `Document::all()`) followed by an in-memory check of the type ... That scope would be wider than the target scope." plan.md's only selection query applies the labels filter; no application-level type check is proposed.
